column1: # Curated `::tele` destinations -- the rooms nothing else in the tree names.
# `tools/gen_tele_table.py` builds the destination table from three automatic
# sources: the world map's surface labels, the world map's per-map origins, and
# the npc spawn roster. Between them they cover every town, landmark and named
# npc. What they cannot cover is a room with no label, no map of its own and no
# static npc -- which is most of the interesting content: an instanced boss lair
# has no roster spawn because its npc is created by a script, and a raid has no
# world-map label because it is not on the world map.
# `coord` is either a coord literal (`0_50_50_22_18`) or, preferably, `^name` --
# a coord constant the server's own content already declares. Naming the
# constant means this file cannot drift from the room it points at, and it is
# the provenance too: `^cerberus_north_spawn` is a tile the Cerberus scripts
# already stand a player on, which is a far better warrant for "Cerberus is
# here" than a number recalled from the live game. The generator hard-fails on a
# constant it cannot resolve, so a renamed constant is a build error rather than
# Rows here take precedence over the automatic sources, and the automatic
# sources are large -- check `::telefind <name>` before adding a row, because a
# name that is already correct does not need to be restated.
# Bosses deliberately absent: Nex, the Corporeal Beast, Zalcano, Wintertodt,
# Tempoross, Theatre of Blood and Tombs of Amascut have no coord constant in
# this tree, and a guessed coord is worse than no entry -- it teleports you
# somewhere confidently wrong. Add them when the content that needs them lands.
